subject: Re: Acme discovery call - TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Acme discovery call - TCO recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and to make sure we’re aligned on next steps. Appreciate you walking us through the integration goals.

Pain points we heard
- Token cost sensitivity: current pilots are running into unexpectedly high per-month inference spend and the team needs predictable unit economics.
- Latency SLOs for customer-facing features: 95th percentile latency target ~300ms for the LLM path.
- Data isolation / retention: audit logs and shorter retention window required for compliance.

Goals we agreed on
- Reduce inference spend to fit within Acme's Q1 budget (target: ~$200k for inference).
- Meet 95th P latency <= 300ms for interactive flows.
- Pilot with 1-2 key endpoints (search rerank + summary) and measure both cost and quality.

High-level token/TCO notes (very rough estimates from today’s usage numbers)
- Current baseline: ~500M tokens/month across prod+staging (avg. prompt+completion ~1.2k tokens).
- Redwood hosted estimate (baseline model variant): ~$0.08 per 1k tokens -> baseline monthly = ~$40k. (Note: this is a placeholder estimate; exact model and pricing variant will change numbers.)
- Cost reduction levers we discussed:
  - Batching & concurrency tuning: expected 10–25% cost decrease on token throughput for synchronous batchable workloads.
  - Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (search rerank): can reduce effective tokens per call by ~30–60% depending on cache hit rate.
  - Quantized model variants (8-bit / 4-bit): 20–50% cost reduction with small quality tradeoffs for some tasks.

Next steps (proposal)
1) I’ll share a short TCO one-pager and a pricing spreadsheet (attached) that shows three scenarios: baseline, batching+cache, and batching+cache+quantization.
2) Rafael to run a quick knob-check with our infra team on latency SLO tradeoffs for the quantized variants (cc’d).
3) If numbers look good, pilot: 6–8 week pilot on Hosted or Dedicated (we’ll recommend depending on scale/latency).
4) Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra/ML team — Rafael + Monica + one eng will join.

Proposed times for the tech deep-dive: Wed Dec 2, Thu Dec 3, or Fri Dec 4 (10–11am PT or 1–2pm PT). Which works best?

Attaching: acme_tco_onepager.pdf (high level) and redwood_pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenario numbers).

Thanks — happy to adjust these assumptions based on your internal metrics.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: acme_tco_onepager.pdf (PDF, 120KB); redwood_pricing_model.xlsx (Excel, 65KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme discovery call - TCO recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions:

1) Can you break the baseline estimate into prompt vs completion token cost (our average completion is sizeable)?
2) Our Q1 inference budget for this initiative is ~$200k — is that realistic for the scope you laid out?
3) Latency: if we move to quantized variants, what’s the typical delta to 95th P? We can tolerate +50ms but prefer to stay under 300ms.

We’re generally aligned on the pilot approach. Wed Dec 2 at 10am PT works for the deep-dive. I’ll invite our ML infra lead (Sarah) and one product PM.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director of Product, Acme Corp
jordan.blake@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme discovery call - TCO recap & next steps

Great — thanks Jordan, see answers below and attached a slightly updated spreadsheet with the prompt/completion split.

Answers
- Prompt vs completion split: historically for workflows like yours we see ~40% prompt : 60% completion by token count. I updated the spreadsheet to show that split and how it maps to monthly spend across the three scenarios.
- Budget fit: With batching + KV caching we show a scenario that lands ~35–45% below baseline, which should put you within the $200k quarterly budget for pilot scale (spreadsheet shows monthly -> quarterly projection). We’ll refine after we get exact call volumes and cache hit rate.
- Latency with quantized variants: Rafael — short answer is usually +20–70ms on 95th P depending on model and GPU; on A100/RTX-class for small batches it’s often within the +50ms acceptable window. We’ll profile during the pilot.

Next steps confirmed
- Deep-dive: Wed Dec 2, 10–11am PT. Rafael and Monica will join to cover latency profiling and integration surface.
- I’ll prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) after the deep-dive that lists milestones for the pilot, success metrics (cost per 1k tokens, 95th P latency), and responsibilities.

If helpful, we can include a preliminary credit/discount table in the MAP depending on committed monthly tokens for Dedicated. Rafael — can you draft a slug for committed pricing options ahead of Wed?

Thanks — attaching the updated redwood_pricing_model.xlsx with the prompt/completion split and scenario numbers.

—
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pricing_model.xlsx (Excel, 67KB)

Actions for Rafael / Monica:
- Rafael: can you draft 2 committed pricing slugs (monthly token commit tiers) + one-off pilot credit options we can show in the MAP? Include what margin/discount you think is defensible.
- Monica: please prepare a short checklist for the deep-dive covering integration points we need (API keys, VPC options, logging retention, sample payloads).
- Let’s also bring a simple latency profile matrix for quantized vs baseline (95th P) — Rafael, just ballpark numbers are fine for Wed; we’ll profile during pilot.

I’ll finalize the MAP and attach the TCO one-pager before the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa
